messages:
maria: quick question — for the v1->v2 deprecation migration, can the console expose a per-tenant 'grace toggle' so customers can opt out of the automatic header-based routing? worried about customers hitting rate spikes when we autoshift. want minimal SRE involvement.
ajay: we currently only have a global flag in the gateway. per-tenant introduces a lookup on request path which could add cost. that said, we could cache it in the gateway (redis or local TTL) to avoid DB on every request.
sam: from a UX/metrics perspective: if we offer per-tenant toggles we should also show migration health on the tenant page (v1 % vs v2 %, error rate deltas, latency deltas). otherwise folks will flip blindly.
deploy-bot: rollout-bot:canary started for v2-migration at 2025-04-22T18:01:00Z :rocket:
lena: main concern is route-table blowup and stale state. caching helps but TTL tradeoffs matter. also remember quotas: if many tenants stay on v1 we could overload reserved v1 capacity. need quota guardrail.
chris: alternative approach: console exposes a 'grace window' with sampling and a manual 'legacy lock' option. default is sampling 0.5% -> increase if we observe regressions. full opt-out would be manual and require an override (or a support/SRE flow).
maria: i get the SRE-safety argument, but customers will want self-serve. maybe two tiers: a self-serve sampling toggle + requestable full opt-out (support ticket or org-admin approval). telemetry needs to capture 'compat_route' events.
ajay: agree on telemetry. propose schema: event: compat_route { tenant_id, client_version, chosen_route(v1|v2), fallback_reason, request_tokens, latency_ms }. Include billing tags so invoices map to served tokens.
sam: UX nit: in the tenant migration panel show a single line: "migration health — v2 success rate / latency change / rollback risk" and a 3-state button: sample / opt-in / legacy-lock. clicking legacy-lock should surface consequences (quota, no auto-updates).
chris: quick sketch of implementation for gateway:
```
// pseudocode
meta = tenantCache.get(tenant_id)
if meta && meta.legacy_lock == true then route_v1()
else route_by_client_header_or_default()
```
Cache TTL 10m, fallback to metadata store (redis) on miss.
lena: also add a quota circuit that prevents more than X tenants holding legacy_lock concurrently (configurable by account tier). prevents resource exhaustion. we should add a backlog metric for legacy_lock_count per pool.
ajay: action items (rough): 1) telemetry schema PR (sam) 2) console toggle UX mock + copy (sam) 3) gateway prototype caching + TTL 10m (ajay) 4) quota circuit + alert/playbook (lena) 5) docs + billing note (maria) anyone swap?
sam: i'll take 1 and 2. i'll open the telemetry PR with the mock event payload and a sample dashboard.
ajay: i'll prototype gateway caching behavior and perf numbers. will try to keep lookups off happy-path when header present.
lena: i'll design quota circuit + alarm thresholds and draft playbook for when legacy_lock_count > threshold.
maria: great. small question — can we avoid a metadata lookup if client sends "x-redwood-api-version" header? most customers include it. only do tenant lookup when header absent or header==v1 and tenant opted-in to migration.
ajay: yep we can make header-first. that'll keep perf impact minimal for the majority of traffic. good call.
chris: also let's add an event for when console toggles legacy_lock so it's auditable: admin_id, timestamp, reason. adds compliance trace.
maria: love it. thanks. sync to review mocks + telemetry schema WED 10:00am?
sam: yep. i'll post the mock link before EOD tmrw.
lena: will wire up the playbook draft in runbooks repo and link it in the PR.
ajay: prototype branch by Fri.
maria: :thumbsup: thanks team — this should give customers self-serve while keeping SRE guardrails in place.
